pharm: Oral L-glutamine that replenishes intracellular glutamine and reduces oxidative stress in sickle red blood cells.
quick: 10-15 g orally twice daily based on body weight (2-3 packets per dose)
Mix in beverage or soft food; take immediately after mixing, with or without meals

Sickle cell crisis frequency, GI tolerability
summary: L-glutamine (Endari) is an oral amino acid powder indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients 5 years of age and older. Glutamine is a key substrate for synthesis of NAD and NADH, which protect red blood cells from oxidative damage; supplementing it is thought to reduce oxidative stress that contributes to sickling. It is dosed twice daily by body weight (5 g, 10 g, or 15 g per dose) and is mixed into a beverage or soft food immediately before ingestion. It is generally well tolerated, with constipation, nausea, headache, and abdominal pain being the most common adverse effects.
indications: To reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients 5 years of age and older

dosage.n: Total 10 g/day; each packet contains 5 g L-glutamine powder

dosage.c: Sickle cell disease, weight 30 to 65 kg

admin: Mix the prescribed number of packets immediately before ingestion in 8 oz (240 mL) of a cold or room-temperature beverage such as water, milk, or apple juice, or in 4 to 6 oz of food such as applesauce or yogurt
Complete dissolution is not required before administration
Take twice daily; do not take more than the prescribed number of packets per dose
Each packet contains 5 g of L-glutamine as a white crystalline powder
moa: The precise mechanism in sickle cell disease is not fully established. L-glutamine is a precursor for nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD and its reduced form NADH), which play a central role in the redox balance of red blood cells. Sickle red cells have increased oxidative stress and an impaired NADH redox potential; supplemental L-glutamine is thought to improve the NAD redox ratio and reduce oxidative damage, thereby decreasing red-cell sickling and adhesion and reducing the frequency of vaso-occlusive (pain) crises.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to L-glutamine or any component of the product
relative: Severe hepatic impairment (caution; glutamine metabolism may be altered)
monitor: Frequency and severity of sickle cell crises and hospitalizations
Renal and hepatic function in at-risk patients

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of Endari in pregnant women. L-glutamine is an endogenous amino acid; however, data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: There is no information on the presence of L-glutamine from Endari in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established for renal impairment; the safety of supplemental glutamine in significant renal dysfunction has not been well studied, so use with caution and monitor.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is established for hepatic impairment; glutamine contributes to ammonia/nitrogen handling, so use with caution in significant hepatic impairment and monitor.

minor: Lactulose (theoretical: glutamine is metabolized to ammonia, which could counteract ammonia-lowering therapy)
interactions.food: May be mixed with food or beverage; no clinically significant food interaction is described.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol has been described.
interactions.diagnostics: May modestly affect amino acid and ammonia measurements; no specific labeled diagnostic interference.

counsel: Take twice every day, even when feeling well, to help reduce sickle cell pain crises
Mix each dose in a drink or soft food right before taking it; full dissolving is not needed
This medicine does not replace your other sickle cell treatments such as hydroxyurea, hydration, or pain care
Constipation, nausea, and headache are the most common side effects; tell your provider if they are bothersome
Keep packets at room temperature, away from direct sunlight
pk: Clinical benefit (reduced crises) develops over weeks to months of continued use
Plasma glutamine rises within about 30 minutes to a few hours after an oral dose
Short; plasma glutamine half-life on the order of about 1 hour
Requires ongoing twice-daily dosing for sustained benefit
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), away from direct sunlight
pearls: FDA-approved as Endari to reduce acute complications of sickle cell disease in patients aged 5 years and older
Dosed by body weight in 5 g packets: 1, 2, or 3 packets per dose twice daily for <30 kg, 30-65 kg, and >65 kg
Proposed benefit is improving the NAD redox ratio and reducing oxidative stress in sickle red cells
Adjunct therapy; can be used with or without hydroxyurea and does not replace standard sickle cell care
Generally well tolerated; GI complaints (constipation, nausea, abdominal pain) and headache are the main issues
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular twice-daily schedule; do not take a double dose.
overdose: There is no specific experience with Endari overdose. Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal upset (nausea, abdominal discomfort) and, in patients with hepatic impairment, could theoretically raise ammonia. Management is supportive; there is no specific antidote.
